Here are my findings.

## Build system & running tests

- **Maven** (multi-file Maven project). Root: `/home/daniel/sandbox/pom.xml` — `artifactId` = `spring-petclinic-rest`, packaging is a Spring Boot app (`spring-boot-maven-plugin` at line 275). Wrapper present: `/home/daniel/sandbox/mvnw` (and `mvnw.cmd`). There is **no** Gradle build.
- Run the full test suite: `./mvnw test` (from `/home/daniel/sandbox`). Run a single test class: `./mvnw test -Dtest=AcceptanceTest`.
- Note: this is Spring PetClinic REST re-wired to **OfficeFloor function injection** (per `/home/daniel/sandbox/CLAUDE.md`). The `AssignX` classes are OfficeFloor pipeline functions (each has a `service(...)` method with `@Val`-injected parameters); they are auto-discovered/orchestrated, not referenced by name anywhere in `src/main`, so grepping for callers returns nothing.

## 1. Where customerCode is generated (format logic)

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/AssignCustomerCode.java` (lines 13-21):

```java
public class AssignCustomerCode {

    public void service(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository ownerRepository) {
        int sequence = ownerRepository.findAll().size() + 1;
        String lastName = owner.getLastName();
        String last3 = lastName.substring(0, Math.min(3, lastName.length())).toUpperCase();
        owner.setCustomerCode(String.format("%s-%04d", last3, sequence));
    }
}
```

Current format (from the Javadoc, lines 7-12 and the code): `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` — upper-cased first 3 letters of last name, a hyphen, then a **global** 4-digit zero-padded sequence = `ownerRepository.findAll().size() + 1` (e.g. `SMI-0007`). Note it uses `findAll().size()` (a global owner count), not a per-city count.

## 2. Everything derived from customerCode

- **membershipNumber** — `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/AssignMembershipNumber.java` (lines 12-18):

```java
public class AssignMembershipNumber {

    public void service(@Val Owner owner) {
        String yy = String.format("%02d", owner.getRegistrationDate().getYear() % 100);
        owner.setMembershipNumber(owner.getCustomerCode() + "-M" + yy);
    }
}
```

Format `<customerCode>-M<YY>` where YY = last 2 digits of `registrationDate` year (e.g. `SMI-0007-M26`). Javadoc (lines 6-11) notes it runs *after* customer code and registration date are assigned, so changing the customerCode format automatically changes the membershipNumber prefix.

- **membershipTier** — a separate, unrelated derivation in the mapper (NOT from customerCode). `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java` lines 25-26: `"SILVER"` if `namesakeCount == 0` and email non-empty, else `"BRONZE"`. (Also sets `displayName` line 21-22, `initials` line 23-24.)

## 3. Tests referencing customerCode / membership

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java` (whole file, 16 lines):

```java
/** customer-code-city: Change the customerCode format to '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where CITY3 is the upper-cased... */
class AcceptanceTest extends AcceptanceBase {

	@Test
	void coreCustomerCodeHasCityPrefix() throws Exception {
		int id = createOwnerOk(ownerNode());
		JsonNode n = fetchOwner(id);
		assertTrue(n.get("customerCode").asText().matches("[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\\d{4}")); // <CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>
	}
}
```

Important: this test asserts the format `[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}` (`<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`), which the **current** `AssignCustomerCode` (`<LAST3>-<NNNN>`) does **not** satisfy — the test expects a city prefix that the code does not yet produce. This is a target/spec test for an "evolve" task.

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java` — supporting harness (no direct customerCode assertion, but relevant context):
- Line 37 (class Javadoc): mentions "membership number, per-day cap, per-city cap, 'most common city'" as count/quota rules.
- Line 85: comment noting a unique first name "keeps namesakeCount at 0."
- Owner payload builder `ownerNode()` (lines 117-125) sets firstName/lastName/address/**city**/telephone. `fillCity(String city, int n)` (lines 173-179) creates n owners in the same city (drives per-city rules).
- Test isolation: `@SpringBootTest`, `@AutoConfigureMockMvc`, `@Transactional`, `@WithMockUser(...ADMIN)` (lines 47-51). Helper `sha256hex`/`shaHex`/`luhn` (lines 282-321) for derived-value assertions.

## 4. Owner entity and its fields

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` — `@Entity @Table(name="owners")`, extends `Person` (so `firstName`/`lastName` come from the `Person` superclass). Field declarations (lines 38-70):

- `address` (line 38-40, `@NotEmpty`)
- `city` (line 42-44, `@NotEmpty`, column `city`)
- `telephone` (line 46-49, `@NotEmpty`, `@Pattern` E.164 `^\+[0-9]{8,15}$`)
- `email` (line 51-52)
- `registrationDate` : `LocalDate` (line 54-55, column `registration_date`)
- `customerCode` : `String` (line 57-58, column `customer_code`)
- `membershipNumber` : `String` (line 60-61, column `membership_number`)
- `householdId` : `String` (line 63-64, column `household_id`)
- `namesakeCount` : `Integer` (line 66-67, column `namesake_count`)
- `pets` : `Set<Pet>` (line 69-70)

Getters/setters for city at lines 80-86; customerCode 112-118; membershipNumber 120-126; registrationDate 104-110; namesakeCount 136-142; householdId 128-134. `toString()` (204-216) includes lastName, firstName, address, city, telephone.

`lastName`/`firstName` are inherited — see `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Person.java` (referenced by `getLastName()`/`getFirstName()` used throughout).

## 5. OwnerRepository methods (city-count check)

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/OwnerRepository.java` (interface, lines 36-87). Available methods:
- `Collection<Owner> findByLastName(String lastName)` (line 46)
- `Page<Owner> findByLastName(String lastName, Pageable)` (line 48)
- `Owner findById(int id)` (line 57)
- `void save(Owner owner)` (line 66)
- `Collection<Owner> findAll()` (line 74)
- `Page<Owner> findAll(Pageable)` (line 76)
- `void delete(Owner owner)` (line 84)

**There is no count-by-city (or any city-based) method.** To count owners by city today you must call `findAll()` and filter in-memory by `getCity()` (this is exactly how `AssignNamesakeCount` counts namesakes and how `AssignHousehold` finds household members — both iterate `ownerRepository.findAll()`).

Implementations (all implement the same interface, none add a city-count method):
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/jpa/JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl.java` (JPQL; has `SELECT COUNT(owner)` queries only for lastName paging at line 76 and total at line 116).
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/springdatajpa/SpringDataOwnerRepository.java` (Spring Data `@Query`, lines 40-56).
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/jdbc/JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl.java` (raw SQL; note its SELECTs at lines 86/101/125/186/201 only project `id, first_name, last_name, address, city, telephone` — they do **not** load `customer_code`, `membership_number`, `registration_date`, etc.).

- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/AssignNamesakeCount.java` (lines 13-31): counts pre-existing owners with same first+last name via `findAll()` loop; sets `namesakeCount`.

## Summary

The change was localized to one file, because membership number (and all other derived values) are built by concatenating the `customerCode` at runtime rather than storing a copy of the old format.

**`AssignCustomerCode.java`** — changed the format from `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` (global sequence) to `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`:
- **CITY3** — upper-cased first three letters of the owner's city
- **LAST3** — upper-cased first three letters of the last name
- **NNNN** — a *per-city* 4-digit zero-padded sequence: one more than the number of owners already in that city (counted via `findAll()` filtered by normalized city, matching the existing `AssignNamesakeCount`/`AssignHousehold` pattern, since the repository has no count-by-city method).

**No change needed to `AssignMembershipNumber`** — it produces `<customerCode>-M<YY>` by reading `getCustomerCode()`, so it automatically inherits the new city-prefixed format (e.g. `LON-SMI-0001-M26`). That satisfies the "every value derived from the customerCode must be rebuilt on the new format" requirement.

Test result: `AcceptanceTest.coreCustomerCodeHasCityPrefix` (asserting `[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}`) passes, and the full `./mvnw test` run reports **BUILD SUCCESS** with 0 failures/errors.
